newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler won't comment on management revamp report.
newsitem.headline: Daimler won't comment on management revamp report.

text.p: Daimler-Benz AG on Sunday declined comment on a magazine report that management board chairman Juergen Schrempp planned to streamline the management of Germany's biggest industrial group.
News magazine Der Spiegel reported that Schrempp had put forward various radical options for a revamp at an internal management meeting last Thursday.
One of the ideas envisaged removing the management board level at Daimler's large subsidiaries, Spiegel reported in an advance copy of a report to be published in Monday's editions.
Another idea involved transforming Daimler into a pure financial holding company and strengthening the power of subsidiaries, the report said.
Daimler spokesman Roland Klein said in response to a Reuter enquiry that the company never commented on speculation.
The report said any decision on a management reorganization would only be reached by consensus. The ideas represented extreme positions and hence could barely be realized, it added.
Any complete removal of the subsidiaries' management power would be blocked by Helmut Werner, management board chairman of Daimler's flagship unit Mercedes-Benz AG, the report said.
And a transfer of power to subsidiaries would not be in Schrempp's interest, it added.
Daimler spokesman Roland Klein said both Schrempp and Werner have noted that the group will have to think about changes at management board level.
